photos.method: the photograph is turned 7.2 degrees about (730, 270) because the skip stands tilted on a slope (the top rim's slope), then each edge is the strongest grey-level step inside the recorded window on the turned copy; the scale is fitted on the one span from the rim bar's lower edge to the foot (124.4 px for 1114 mm if the skip is 1200 high: 0.1117 px per mm); the height of 1200 is Judgement (it sets the scale), so the proportions are checked and the absolute lengths are judged; the right bottom corner and the top corners are against fence wire and sky and faint, so they are not used; the tolerance is the measured spread times 3 plus 2 px, at least 6 px (54 mm)

sources.author: the Secretary of State for Transport and the Secretary of State for Wales (a statutory instrument: The Builders' Skips (Markings) Regulations 1984, SI 1984/1933)
sources.taken: 1984-12-11 (made; in force 21 January 1985; the marking required from 1 January 1986)
sources.shows: every end of a builder's skip any part of which stands on a highway other than a footway or verge must from 1 January 1986 carry a marking of two plates of equal size and shape (BS AU 152: 1970, the rear marking plate standard), red fluorescent stripes and yellow reflex-reflecting ground as Schedule 1's diagram shows (each plate 140 to 280 wide, 350 to 700 long, area at least 980 square cm, stripes 40 to 50 degrees to the vertical and 133 to 147 broad, rising toward the inner edge); Schedule 2 places them: as near an outer edge as the skip allows, innermost edges equidistant from the skip's axis, upper edges level with each other and not lower than the skip's upper edge unless the construction needs it, at most 1.5 m above the ground, never on a lid, on a door only if nowhere else will do
sources.not_used_for: BS AU 152 itself (not freely readable: the plate's own small marking is a Judgement); no picture
sources.period: in force in 1990: a skip in Quay Street's road carries these plates on both ends

regulation.title: The Builders' Skips (Markings) Regulations 1984 (SI 1984/1933), made 11 December 1984 under s.139(4) of the Highways Act 1980, in force 21 January 1985; the marking required from 1 January 1986
regulation.read: 2026-10-13: the made text and the original print PDF (Schedule 1's diagram, page 5686)
regulation.standard: BS AU 152: 1970 (rear marking plates for vehicles); the Standard itself was not read

chosen.stripe_rise: toward the plate's inner edge (the two plates of an end make a chevron pointing up, as Schedule 1's two halves do)
chosen.pattern: plate frame: v down from the upper edge, d from the inner edge; red where ((v - d x tan 45) - 70) mod 280 lies within 70 of zero, yellow elsewhere; the first stripe at the upper edge is partial, as in the diagram; a 2 mm yellow border
chosen.size_reason: the upper end plate is 535 mm along its slope and 422 mm of it lie under the rim bar's lower edge: a 380 long plate fits with 38 mm to spare, 270 wide takes 1026 square cm, over the 980 minimum
chosen.mark_text: the Standard's paragraph 5 marking (BS AU 152 and a maker's mark) was not read: a small 'BS AU 152' in 8 mm capitals on the lower yellow margin is a Judgement, with no maker's mark

marking.diagram: Schedule 1 shows two halves, mirror images: stippled stripes (red fluorescent) alternate with unstippled (yellow reflex), 40 to 50 degrees to the vertical, 133 to 147 broad measured up the plate; each half 140 to 280 wide and 350 to 700 long; the stripes rise toward the inner edges, so the two plates of an end make a chevron pointing up

placement.slot: west carriageway, the long side parallel to the kerb, centre x 22.5 m (in front of the yard mouth, x 21 to 24), 0.30 m from the kerb face (the skip's near side at z -2.70, its centre line at z -1.85), the firm's name and the lamps on the road side (street +z); its floor lies on the road's camber, tilted 1.4 degrees with the kerb side low; the south end (street -x) faces the hook camera with two striped marking plates on each end

cones_optional.note: if cones are wanted at the skip's road ends they stand in the carriageway on the skip's centre line, 0.2 to 0.3 m beyond its ends; the scene's own cones stay where they are (on the west footway); the cones are off the drawn street since 3 October (terrace-front.py HELD_PROPS_OFF_STREET)

tilt.rule: the floor lies on the road's camber (1 in 40) and tilts with it, so the builder neither sinks one side into the road nor floats the other (42 mm across the 1690 width)

accent.method: pinhole projection of the skip's parts at its pose into the hook camera (x -3, z -1.6, eye 2.2 m above the crown, yaw 20.4, pitch -3.4 up, 46 degrees vertical, 16:9), nothing in front hiding it, so an upper bound; a projection of this target's own parts, not a render
accent.verdict: about 0.4 percent of the frame against the 7.8 percent ceiling of art-direction R-B4 (the frame's share above saturation 0.6): small, so the sample stays yellow; the orange and faded blue-green stay colour variants

reasons: the 2 October ruling took the skip off the street 'until real'; the scene's story ('the yard is shut': a barrier across the mouth, cones, a skip) places it before the yard mouth, one event with the pallets behind the barrier (the pallets target)

the near lane is 3.0 m: a skip 1700 mm wide at 0.30 m from the kerb leaves 3.0 - 0.30 - 1.70 = 1.0 m in its own lane and the whole 3.0 m other lane: the street stays passable (2.8 m is the least a bus needs; cars are off in any case); the shared placement rows measure the widest free width across the road
its length is 3.0 m, the width of the yard mouth: it fills the street frontage of the gap without crossing a shop front

THE CONES DO NOT MOVE. The first version moved the scene's two cones to x 20.7 and 24.3 on a misreading: they stand on the west FOOTWAY, 0.35 m behind the kerb face (vignette-pieces.json prop_traffic_cone_01_0 and _02_0 at z -3.35), not inside the skip's length; the skip (z -2.70 to -1.00) does not touch them, and cones moved to x 20.7 and 24.3 at that depth would stand inside the bollards there (prop_decorative_bollard_02_0 and _1, z -3.40 to -3.60). If cones are wanted at the skip's road ends they go at z -1.85, in the carriageway on the skip's centre line, at x 20.7 and 24.3; the cones are off the drawn street since 3 October

a skip on the highway needs lamps at night and a permit: the two amber lamps are on the skip; the double yellow lines (0.25 m from the kerb) lie under it: a skip on the lines is a street fact (a permit, Judgement)

a skip any part of which stands on the carriageway carried, from 1 January 1986, a marking of two striped plates on each end (SI 1984/1933, S8): the south end faces the hook camera, about 24 m away and 20 degrees off its axis, well inside the frame, so four striped plates are among the first things a 1990 skip in the road shows; they are on the upper end plates, level with each other (their upper edges 4 mm under the rim bar, about 1.1 m above the road), 270 wide, 380 long, 5 mm inside the end's outer edges and mirror images about the skip's axis
the floor lies on the road's camber: 1 in 40 is 1.43 degrees, the kerb side low, 42 mm across the 1690 width

wear: yellow paint chalked, dented along the rim and the lower plates (a hundred dents 20 to 80 mm, seeds), chipped to rust at the rim's top edge and the lugs, rust runs 30 to 120 mm below the chipped places
mud and cement to knee height (a mask from the floor up, 0.4 m on the side plates), black tar and bitumen splashes, lime-white splashes
the stencilled name worn, a few letters chipped; the paint on the end plates scraped by the lorry's chains
the lamps: dirty lenses, one cracked (a seed)

the four end marking plates: scuffed and dirt-streaked (the regulation asks them to be clean and efficient, so a dirty one is a street fact, not the target), the fluorescent red faded toward orange-red, one plate cracked across a corner (a seed), mud splashes on the lowest 100 mm
contents: empty in the sample (a variant carries a heap of plasterboard, bricks and timber lath, never a person or a drink container: a seed in the builder's decals)
NOT shown: a real firm's name or number, a person, any drink container
